name: chamfered_shaft_does_not_dimension_the_legs
why: ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF 27/9/2026, findings on the round part. A Ø30 shaft 40 long with a 1 x 45° chamfer at both ends. From the end the circles are two: the Ø30 (cone-cylinder) and the Ø28 (cone-plane, the edge of the chamfer), and the second is not a diameter to dimension. From the side the circles seen edge-on are four (at 0, 1, 39, 40): counted all as faces, the lengths 1, 39 and 40 were born — the «legs» of the chamfer, which the rest of the drawing discards. A face of the round part is a circle that borders a PLANAR face perpendicular to the axis. And the Ø30 dimensioned from the end is the same CYLINDER that from the side is not dimensioned twice (the key belongs to the cylinder, not to the diameter alone).
defect_caught: The legs of the chamfer dimensioned as lengths of the round part; the edge of a chamfer dimensioned as an outer diameter; the same diameter dimensioned in two views.
_the_views_are_called_by_uid: V1 front (the shaft from the side), V3 side (the shaft from the end).

expect.tolerance_why: pi inside: pi x 15^2 x 40 minus two chamfer rings (pi x 15^2 x 1 minus the truncated cone pi/3 x (15^2 + 15 x 14 + 14^2))

expect.why: the diameter of the shaft, re-read
the edge of the chamfer is stated, not dimensioned as a diameter
the only length: between the two flat ends. No 1 and 39
the Ø30 is already dimensioned from the end: the same cylinder, only once

no dimension of 30 is born in this view: the Ø30 is from the end. The first run (28/9/2026) also asked that it say so among those already dimensioned: from the side SOLIDWORKS does not expose a pair of generatrices of the Ø30 squeezed between the two chamfers (like the Ø20 of the stepped shaft), so there is nothing to attempt and nothing to say. What matters is that a duplicate is not born.
